absent: PAR's Latin American roots (Fals-Borda, Freire) are absent despite the participatory topic; Santos is not cited.
forYou: A direct Tsing lineage for your CARN workshop: Friction (2005) → Demeulenaere's 'transformative frictions' (2014) → this paper. Long's 'battlefields of knowledge' is a useful older ally for the substrate argument.
method: References from Crossref; strands and narrative by Claude, grounded only in the reference list and title.
narrative: Two older roots meet here. From development studies comes the farmer-first tradition: Chambers' 'Putting the last first' (1983) and Richards' 'Indigenous agricultural revolution' (1985). From rural sociology comes Norman Long's actor-oriented view that knowledge is made at 'interfaces' between actors (1989, 1992).

Agrawal's 1995 critique of the indigenous/scientific divide sets the debate the paper answers. Its own frame comes from Tsing's 'Friction' (2005), which gives the title, and Haraway's situated knowledges (1988).
It is positioned in the transdisciplinary literature (Max-Neef; Pohl; Polk; Scholz), with a thin but explicit power strand (Gaventa's power cube; Fritz on power in TD).
